results.title: Ghana’s nuclear journey: From Nkrumah’s vision to a new investment commitment
results.content: Ghana’s proposed US$200 million investment in nuclear power readiness marks a significant step in a journey that began more than six decades ago. It renews an ambition rooted in the country’s earliest development agenda: building the energy capacity to sustain industrialisation and economic transformation. During a recent discussion in the media, I expressed support for this investment. Its importance becomes clearer when placed within the history of Ghana’s efforts to include nuclear power in its electricity generation mix. In 1961, under President Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana decided to undertake the Ghana Nuclear Reactor Project. Its immediate purpose was to establish a research reactor for scientific research, training and radioisotope production. results.title: Child Online Africa calls for AU action on online violence against children
results.content: Child Online Africa has called on the African Union (AU) and its member states to take urgent and coordinated action to protect children from online violence, sexual exploitation and other forms of digital abuse. The organisation has launched the #AfricaESafetyNow campaign ahead of the Second Global Ministerial Conference on Ending Violence Against Children, scheduled for November 18 to 19, 2026, in Manila, Philippines. In a statement issued on Tuesday, November 17, the organisation said Africa had reached a critical point in addressing the risks children face as they increasingly engage with digital platforms.
